title: Deprecation safety-net: traffic replayer, probe suite, and migration scaffolding for API behavior flags
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood is introducing behavior flags and versioned API contracts for streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. To avoid customer regressions we need a reproducible safety-net that can detect semantic and latency regressions before we flip flags broadly.

Goal:
Build a combined test + production replay capability (Traffic Replayer), a small automated probe suite for common regression classes, and lightweight migration scaffolding (prompts, schema shims, and customer-facing migration notes) so engineers and PMs can safely deprecate legacy behaviors with measurable guardrails.

Scope (this ticket):
- Implement Traffic Replayer service to replay sampled production requests against candidate behavior-flag configurations (non-intrusive, read-only).
- Create a standard Probe Suite that detects: streaming truncation/regression, function/tool-call JSON schema drift, tokenization/structured-output schema mismatches, latency regressions under batching.
- Integrate probe and replayer outputs into Console as a compatibility heatmap and per-route regression alerts.
- Add migration scaffolding templates (prompt diffs, structured-output mappings) for PM/Docs to convert into customer migration guides.

Out of scope:
- Global automated flag flips (will be a follow-up after we validate mitigations).
- Long-term retention of replay payloads beyond 14 days (compliance team restriction).

Risks & trade-offs:
- Privacy: replaying production payloads risks exposing PII. Trade-off: replayer will run in read-only mode inside the Dedicated/Private control plane and scrub known sensitive fields using existing PII-scrubber libraries. Will require security sign-off.
- Cost: replays consume compute. We will sample traffic (0.5% baseline adjustable per route) and prioritize high-traffic routes and customer-efficacy routes.
- False positives: some regressions are downstream (model nondeterminism). Probes combine behavioral assertions with statistical baselines to reduce noise.

Notes on streaming & tool-calls specifics:
- Streaming: probe asserts that streaming chunks arrive in order, with no unexpected truncation, and that tokens per-second metrics do not degrade beyond configured SLO delta. Also verify function call boundaries are emitted the same way (start/call/end events).
- Function/tool calling: replayer runs the request up to the point of a tool call and then instead of invoking external systems, we replay the recorded tool invocation payloads (saved in the original request trace) to validate the call signature and response handling.
- Structured outputs: probes validate JSON schema compatibility and provide a lightweight shim engine that maps deprecated keys to new schema when safe (configurable per-route).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Traffic Replayer service implemented and can replay sampled requests for at least 3 representative routes (chat, streaming generation, embedding-to-rerank).
2) Probe Suite has 6 canonical probes: streaming-truncation, streaming-order, function-call-signature, structured-output-schema, latency-batch-regression, kv-cache-behavior.
3) Console compatibility heatmap shows pass/fail per-route with historical baselines.
4) Automated alerts trigger when regression rate > 0.5% for a route or average P95 latency increases by >10% vs baseline.
5) Security review completed and PII-scrubbing is enabled; compliance checklist signed.
6) Migration scaffolding templates created and reviewed by PM/Docs; at least one customer-facing migration guide drafted for a deprecation example.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal-only): enable replayer in internal clusters and run against sandboxed candidate flags for 2 weeks to collect baselines. Recruit 2 platform customers for closed alpha (opt-in).
Phase 2 (beta): enable per-route sampling at 0.5% for low-risk routes; surface heatmap and per-route flags in Console. Run daily automated probe runs and weekly aggregated reports.
Phase 3 (gate): if probes show <0.5% regression and no P0 incidents for 30 days, enable limited canary flips for internal traffic; PM to coordinate customer communication for public deprecation dates.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for replayer core and scrubber.
- Integration test that replays a recorded trace and validates identical parsing and function-call signature detection.
- E2E test harness: run stored production traces against both old and new behavior flags and assert probe pass/fail lists.
- Regression lab: nightly job that runs 5k stored traces and reports diffs; results stored in S3 and linked from Console.
- Backcompat matrix: matrix of client SDK versions vs API flags to ensure minimum supported clients are exercised.
rollback_plan:
- If probe alerts cross thresholds or customers report regressions, immediately disable the candidate behavior-flag in the affected region via rollout policy (console toggle).
- Replayer and probe outputs will provide the failing trace IDs and CSV of failing assertions to speed root-cause.
- If flag disablement insufficient, rolling deploy of previous runtime binary (runtime-1.19) as per infra runbook.
